title: Symmetry and repeating patterns in art around the world

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Look at a butterfly, a flower or a carpet. They all have patterns, and people in every country love making them. Patterns come in three main kinds. Look at the board and let us sort them together.

draw.text: Symmetry and repeating patterns in art around the world

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Look at the first group, mirror symmetry. Fold it down the middle and both halves match, like butterfly wings, the front of the Taj Mahal in India, or the cut paper flags of Mexico called papel picado. Can you find mirror symmetry on your own face?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Now the middle group, turning symmetry. Turn it part of the way round and it looks the same, like a rangoli, a round church rose window, or a Japanese family crest called a kamon. How many turns does a flower with five petals have?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: The last group is repeating patterns: one shape or block, used again and again. Ghana's woven Kente cloth, Indonesian batik and Roman mosaic floors all repeat. Which pattern do you see on your clothes today?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Wonderful sorting! Now make your own repeating pattern. Look at the board and follow the steps. Wow fact: Indonesian batik is so treasured that UNESCO lists it as world heritage. Challenge: fold paper, cut a shape, and open it to see mirror symmetry!

steps.label: Pick a shape
steps.note: A leaf, a star or a zigzag

steps.label: Repeat in a row
steps.note: Draw it again and again, evenly spaced

steps.label: Flip or turn it
steps.note: Try every other one upside down

steps.label: Colour in order
steps.note: Red, blue, red, blue keeps the rhythm

faq.a: Mirror symmetry, or reflective symmetry, means one half is a mirror image of the other, so if you fold along a line, the two halves match exactly.
asks: What is a line of symmetry?

faq.a: Rotational symmetry means a shape looks the same after being turned part of the way round its centre. A five-petal flower looks the same five times in one full turn.
asks: What is the order of rotational symmetry?

faq.a: A repeating pattern uses the same shape, colour or design again and again in a regular way, like stripes, tiles or printed cloth.
asks: What is a pattern in art?
How do I make a repeating pattern?

faq.a: Kente is a colourful woven cloth from Ghana, made of narrow strips woven on looms and sewn together. Its bold repeating patterns and colours carry meanings.
Batik is a way of decorating cloth, famous in Indonesia, where hot wax is drawn on fabric so the dye cannot reach those parts, making beautiful repeating patterns.
asks: Why is batik famous in Indonesia?

facts: UNESCO inscribed Indonesian batik on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009.
A shape with rotational symmetry of order 4 looks the same four times in one full turn.

quiz.say: You fold a butterfly picture down the middle and both halves match. What kind of symmetry is that?
quiz.why: Matching halves along a fold line is mirror, or reflective, symmetry.

wrong.1: Rotational symmetry is about turning, not folding.
wrong.2: The halves match, so it is symmetrical.

quiz.say: Which is an example of a repeating pattern?
quiz.why: Kente cloth repeats its woven shapes and colours again and again.

wrong.2: A blank page has no pattern at all.
